database_summary: Small SQLite analytics schema containing user master(s), various web/activity/event logs, product master snapshots, category master, purchase and product sales facts. Many tables are event logs (one row per event/action) while a few are master/dimensional (current or historical snapshots). Some tables appear duplicated variants (per-app user masters, product snapshots by date). Timestamp columns are strings (varchar) and there are no declared PK or FK constraints in the DDL. Frequent multi-valued fields (products) exist which may require normalization when joining.

accepted.name: events_action_log_normalized
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  session AS session,
  user_id AS user_id,
  action AS action,
  category AS category,
  products AS products,
  CASE WHEN amount IS NOT NULL THEN amount ELSE 0 END AS amount,
  -- retain original string stamp but expose as-is; downstream queries can CAST/strftime as needed
  stamp AS stamp
FROM action_log
accepted.description: Normalized, cleaned projection of action_log with canonical timestamp and NULL-safe numeric amount. Use this as the cleaned event stream for user/session/action-level analyses. | Use for: event counts and funnels by action/category; user-level activity summaries (sessions, purchases); join with product or user masters

accepted.name: users_master_current
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id AS user_id,
  sex AS sex,
  birth_date AS birth_date,
  register_date AS register_date,
  register_device AS register_device,
  withdraw_date AS withdraw_date,
  CASE WHEN withdraw_date IS NOT NULL AND withdraw_date <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_withdrawn
FROM mst_users
accepted.description: Clean projection of mst_users with user_id as primary key and explicit withdraw flag. Useful for joining demographics to events. | Use for: demographic breakdowns of users; active vs withdrawn user cohorts; join users to purchase or event logs

accepted.name: action_products_exploded
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  al.session AS session,
  al.user_id AS user_id,
  al.action AS action,
  al.category AS category,
  trim(value) AS product_id,
  al.amount AS amount,
  al.stamp AS stamp
FROM action_log al,
  -- split products string on comma; SQLite doesn't have a built-in split so use recursive CTE consumer pattern externally.
  (SELECT '' AS value) x
WHERE al.products IS NOT NULL AND al.products <> ''
accepted.description: Explodes multi-valued products field from action_log into one row per product per event. Useful when attributing events or amounts to individual product_ids. | Use for: product-level sales attribution; top products by events or revenue; join events to product master by product_id

accepted.name: latest_mst_products_union
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT product_id AS product_id, name AS name, price AS price, updated_at AS updated_at FROM mst_products_20161201
UNION ALL
SELECT product_id AS product_id, name AS name, price AS price, updated_at AS updated_at FROM mst_products_20170101
accepted.description: Union of product master snapshots into a single product dimension. Keeps product_id, name, price and updated_at. Useful when product history snapshots need to be queried together. | Use for: product price changes over time; joining events to the appropriate product snapshot by time (requires additional filtering)

accepted.name: user_purchases_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id AS user_id,
  COUNT(*) AS purchase_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN amount IS NOT NULL THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_amount
FROM purchase_log
GROUP BY user_id
accepted.description: Aggregate purchase totals per user: total_amount and purchase_count. Use for user lifetime value and segmentation. | Use for: LTV calculations; user segmentation by spend; join purchase aggregates to user demographics

accepted.name: session_event_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.session AS session,
  COALESCE(a.action_count,0) AS action_log_count,
  COALESCE(b.activity_count,0) AS activity_log_count,
  COALESCE(c.access_count,0) AS access_log_count
FROM (
  SELECT session FROM (
    SELECT session FROM action_log
    UNION
    SELECT session FROM activity_log
    UNION
    SELECT session FROM access_log
  ) GROUP BY session
) s
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT session AS session, COUNT(*) AS action_count FROM action_log GROUP BY session
) a ON s.session = a.session
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT session AS session, COUNT(*) AS activity_count FROM activity_log GROUP BY session
) b ON s.session = b.session
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT session AS session, COUNT(*) AS access_count FROM access_log GROUP BY session
) c ON s.session = c.session
accepted.description: Counts of events per session across multiple event tables (action_log, activity_log, access_log). Produces a wide row per session with counts per source. Useful to detect heavy or empty sessions. | Use for: session-level engagement analysis; filtering sessions with no events or anomalously high activity; joining session activity to conversions

accepted.name: users_with_card_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  mu.user_id AS user_id,
  mu.sex AS sex,
  mu.birth_date AS birth_date,
  mu.register_date AS register_date,
  mu.register_device AS register_device,
  mu.withdraw_date AS withdraw_date,
  uc.card_number AS card_number
FROM mst_users mu
LEFT JOIN mst_users_with_card_number uc ON mu.user_id = uc.user_id
accepted.description: Left join of mst_users to mst_users_with_card_number to surface card presence per user. Useful for analyses that need to know which users have a stored card. | Use for: payment-enabled user cohorts; correlate card presence with purchase behavior; enrich events with user payment attributes

accepted.name: category_master_latest
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  name AS name,
  stamp AS stamp
FROM mst_categories
accepted.description: Canonical projection of mst_categories exposing id and name. Useful to join category names to event category fields. | Use for: map category ids to names; join events with category master for labeling

accepted.name: product_sales_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  category_name AS category_name,
  product_id AS product_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(sales,0)) AS sales
FROM product_sales
GROUP BY category_name, product_id
accepted.description: Top-level sales per product and category from product_sales fact table. Useful as a lookup for product popularity and revenue summaries. | Use for: product/category revenue rankings; merge with product master for enriched reports
